---
title: 5 - Vector styles
---

You will use feature attributes to style different forest-reserve categories with different colours, then create a hatch pattern for the national parks and conservation areas layer.

## 5.1. Style forest reserves by category

The *Tanzania Forest Rerserves 2022* layer contains a `desig` attribute (short for *designation*) that defines four sub-categories of different forest reserves:

- `Forest Reserve`
- `Forest Plantation`
- `Nature Forest Reserve`
- `Village Land Forest Reserve`

At the moment, all features in this layer use the same style. We will define a style for each category and then tell OpenLayers which style to use for each feature.

- [ ] Open `main.js`.
- [ ] Make three more imports:

```javascript
import Style from 'ol/style/Style.js';
import Fill from 'ol/style/Fill.js';
import Stroke from 'ol/style/Stroke.js';
```

- [ ] Still working in `main.js`, copy the code block below and paste it just after the imports:

```javascript

// Forest reserve styles based on the 'desig' attribute
const forestStyles = {
  'Forest Reserve': new Style({
    fill: new Fill({
      color: '#000000'
    }),
    stroke: new Stroke({
      color: '#000000',
      width: 1
    })
  }),

  'Forest Plantation': new Style({
    fill: new Fill({
      color: '#000000'
    }),
    stroke: new Stroke({
      color:'#000000',
      width: 1
    })
  }),

  'Nature Forest Reserve': new Style({
    fill: new Fill({
      color: '#000000'
    }),
    stroke: new Stroke({
      color: '#000000',
      width: 1
    })
  }),

  'Village Land Forest Reserve': new Style({
    fill: new Fill({
      color: '#000000'
    }),
    stroke: new Stroke({
      color: '#000000',
      width: 1
    })
  })
};
```

As you can see, each category is displayed separately, and contains parameters for

- `fill` that controls the polygon interior,
- `stroke` that controls the polygon outline, and
- `width` that controls the outline thickness. 

At the moment, the fill and outline colors are black for all categories. 

- [ ] Change the colors for each category's **fill AND stroke** based on the HEX color codes below.
- [ ] After changing the colors, save the `main.js`.
____
* Forest Reserve: `#006b00`
* Forest Plantation: `#d3f226`
* Nature Forest Reserve: `#81bf00`
* Village Land Forest Reserve: `#56cf68`




## 5.2. Apply the style to each feature

Defining the styles does not automatically apply them anywhere. We need a function that reads the `desig` attribute from each feature and returns the matching style.

- [ ] Still in `main.js`, add this function immediately after the previous code where you defined `const forestStyles = {}`:

```javascript
function forestReserveStyleFunction(feature) {
  return forestStyles[feature.get('desig')] || null;
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
`feature.get('desig')` reads the value of the `desig` attribute. The function uses that value to look up the matching style. If no matching category exists, `null` leaves the feature without this style rather than causing the lookup to fail.
:::


## 5.3. Match the style with correct layer

So far, your new style is defined and exists, but it is not added on any vector layer.

- [ ] In `main.js`, scroll down to the `layers` array where you have defined the GeoJSON layers. Here, you'll need to add one additional parameter that tells the `tanzania_forest_reserves_2022.json` to use the style you just created:

```javascript
main.js

  new VectorLayer({
    source: new VectorSource({
      format: new GeoJSON(),
      url: './data/tanzania_forest_reserves_2022.json'
    }),
    style: forestReserveStyleFunction
  }),
```

- [ ] Save and check how the webmap looks like. Do you distinguish the different forest reserve categories?


## 5.4. Create style for the National parks layer

Colours are useful for distinguishing categories, but patterns can also help differentiate overlapping polygon layers. The *Tanzania World Heritage and Ramsar Sites 2026* WMS layer already uses a diagonal hatch pattern, drawn to your map from its styling in GeoServer. 

We will create a similar pattern for *Tanzania National parks and Conservation areas 2023*, but using the opposite diagonal direction. When these two layers overlap, there will be a "net" pattern displayed on the map.

- [ ] Copy the function below and paste it to your `main.js` file, right after the `forestReserveStyleFunction`:

```javascript
// Create a diagonal hatch pattern used to symbolize national parks and conservation areas
function createHatchPattern() {
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  canvas.width = 10;
  canvas.height = 10;

  const context = canvas.getContext('2d');

  //Draw diagonal hatch line
  context.strokeStyle = '#000000';
  context.lineWidth = 1;

  context.beginPath();
  context.moveTo(0, 0);
  context.lineTo(10, 10);
  context.stroke();

  return context.createPattern(canvas, 'repeat');
}

const nationalParksStyle = new Style({
  fill: new Fill({
    color: createHatchPattern()
  }),
  stroke: new Stroke({
    color: '#000000',
    width: 1
  })
});
```

The function draws a short diagonal line on a tiny canvas. `createPattern(..., 'repeat')` repeats that canvas to fill the polygon.

::: {.callout-note}
This is not the most handy way to create diagonal line pattern fills for polygons in OpenLayers, but works well enough for this purpose. For reference, **plugins created by OpenLayers user developers** are a great way to simplify the creation of advanced styles - and streamline the development of many other webmap features, too.
:::

- [ ] Assign this new style to the `tanzania_national_parks_2023.json` layer in the same way as you did for the `tanzania_forest_reserves_2022.json` layer.
- [ ] Save and view the changes on your local development server URL.


![*Our webmap starts to look like - well, a webmap!*](images/5-4_visualised-layers.png)


::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint

Before continuing, make sure that:

- Forest reserve categories have different colours.
- National parks use a hatch pattern.
- The map still loads without JavaScript errors.

If all forest reserves have the same colour, or some of the polygons appear transparent, check the spelling and capitalisation of the `desig` categories. Attribute values must match the keys in `forestStyles` exactly.
:::
